text:
ryan: Pushed an nsys trace from staging (1xA100, 8k seq, batch=4). Something odd — one small kernel is taking almost half the wall time even though SM util is ~30%. Link: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/2285007777 :thinking_face:

maria: which kernel is it? summary pls 

ryan: top hotspots (nsys summary):
```
KernelName                         Calls  TotalTime(ms)  %
attn_fwd_hybrid_vec128                 12        420.3     48.2
kv_prefetch_hook                       48        120.5     13.8
softmax_blocked                        12         80.1      9.2
quant_gemm_tail                        12         60.7      7.0
kv_apply_patch                         24         50.9      5.8
```
But look at SM occupancy and warp efficiency for attn_fwd_hybrid_vec128 — occupancy=0.27, warp_eff=69% and a high warp-issue-stall on mempipe.

alex: low occupancy + high runtime suggests each launch is underfilled (too many registers or shared mem). Could be kernel compiled with high launch bounds for batch shape. Any PTX logs?

ryan: attaching perfetto timeline snapshot: https://perfetto.internal/redwood/view/2285007777 — you can see attn kernel launches back-to-back with long gaps where the GPU is waiting on mem copies from KV cache prefetch. Looks like kv_prefetch_hook is async but still blocks L2 thrashing.

jordan: quick hypotheses:
- attn kernel has high register usage -> low active warps -> low occupancy
- KV prefetch generates hot L2 lines causing cache thrash -> DRAM stalls in attn kernel
- vectorized 128-bit loads (vec128) reintroduce unaligned accesses for short sequences -> serialization

maria: can you rerun with environment variables to force different codegen? try: 
```
export NVCC_TUNE=sm80 && export FORCE_VEC128=0
nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,cudnn -o /tmp/trace2 ./run_infer --seq_len 8 --batch 4
```
I want to see if switching to vec64 + different launch bounds changes register pressure and occupancy.

ryan: running now, will post results in ~30m. Also double-checking kernel compile flags that the runtime picks for this model variant — we have a code path that chooses vec128 for larger seqs, maybe a heuristic bug.

perf-bot: FYI — recent deploy (2024-11-02) updated batching heuristic: prefer smaller micro-batches to reduce latency. This can increase number of kernel launches and hurt occupancy for big-attn kernels. :robot_face:

alex: ah that's interesting. If the batching heuristic split caused many tiny launches, the kernel overhead and register deadzones could amplify. For now, quick mitigations:
- revert micro-batch split for this workload class (seq<16, heads>=16)
- patch KV prefetch to use coarse-grained prefetch (reduce frequency)
- add a fallback codegen path forcing launch bounds for attn_fwd_hybrid to increase active warps

jordan: also instrument nvprof/cuobjdump to dump register usage per kernel:
```
nvdisasm --dump-sass libkernels.so | grep -A3 attn_fwd_hybrid
cuobjdump --dump-elfinfo libkernels.so --device=0
```
That will confirm register/shared mem counts.

maria: if we need a quick test, try disabling kv cache prefetch (RUNTIME_KV_PREFETCH=0) — that should reduce L2 churn and let us see attn-only behavior.

ryan: notes from rerun (after env tweak):
- attn_fwd_hybrid_vec128 runtime dropped to 310ms (from 420ms) and occupancy climbed to 0.44.
- kv_prefetch_hook still shows spikes but less overlap.
So vec64 path helped, but still higher-than-expected per-call time.

alex: good signal. Next steps:
1) Create a small reproducer to iterate quickly (single-layer attention with same dims).
2) Add unit test to batch heuristic that prevents excessive micro-splitting for long-head dims.
3) Run nvdisasm to confirm register pressure and try pragma/tweak to reduce registers (e.g., limit unrolling).
4) Consider kernel fusion: fuse kv_prefetch_hook into attn kernel to avoid kernel-to-kernel syncs (but only if correctness/perf validated).

jordan: I'll own the reproducer and nvdisasm step, ping me if anyone needs a debug build.

ryan: tagging @maria @alex — I'll open an issue with trace links + quick perf diff. If we see regressions in prod, rollback batching heuristic change. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — please include the nvdisasm output in the issue and the perfetto screenshots. Also add check in the CI gating that runs a small latency/throughput profile for critical shapes on deploy.

perf-bot: note added to incident tracker IR-4382 for follow-up.

ryan: will do. Closing thread for now, follow-up in the GH issue. :rocket:
